stem: How did President Wilson justify his request for a declaration of war?

options.label: A
options.text: Wilson demonstrated that the U.S. military was superior to that of the Germans.

options.label: B
options.text: Wilson stated that the Germans had violated the rights of neutral countries.

options.label: C
options.text: Wilson suggested that other countries would aid the U.S. military effort.

options.label: D
options.text: Wilson expressed that Americans had opposed remaining neutral.

visual_elements:
Excerpt from President Woodrow Wilson’s Message to Congress, April 2, 1917:

I have called the Congress into extraordinary session because there are serious . . . choices of policy to be made. . . .

. . . The Imperial German Government . . . use[d] its submarines to sink every vessel that sought to approach either the ports of Great Britain and Ireland or the western coasts of Europe. . . .

It is a war against all nations. American ships have been sunk, American lives taken . . . but the ships and people of other neutral and friendly nations have been sunk and overwhelmed in the waters in the same way. There has been no discrimination. The challenge is to all mankind.
